dedupe_keys.name: temporary flood water storage polders on agricultural land in the middle tisza basin

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes Hungary's flood strategy for the Middle Tisza, where nineteenth-century regulation shortened the river by over 400 km and cut the floodplain by over 90 percent, and peak levels rose from 753 cm in 1876 to 1,040 cm in 2000. After the 1998-2000 floods, dike strengthening was followed by a 2004 plan to give room to the river: agricultural land in temporary reservoirs (polders) is flooded under control to cut the peaks of floods of 100-year return period or more, with a long-term capacity of 721 million cubic metres. Six reservoirs were built in 2009-2015 and another in 2022, at about 260 million euros with European Regional Development Fund and Cohesion Fund support. Farmers receive an upfront payment and event-based damage compensation. An ex-post cost-benefit analysis found the six-reservoir scenario a good trade-off between risk reduction and investment, and a 2022 analysis found most reservoirs justified even for 20-30 year floods. The page, published in 2023 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with references to EPI-WATER. Caveats: farmers were not involved in design, compensation is slow and incomplete, and current land use limits more frequent use. It illustrates nature-based flood hazard reduction, investment appraisal and climate adaptation of river defences; related records are the Kruibeke Bazel Rupelmonde and Lower Danube Green Corridor case studies and GloFAS.
name: Temporary flood water storage polders on agricultural land in the Middle Tisza basin
outcomes: Seven temporary storage polders now cut flood peaks for downstream cities, and analysis shows most would pay off even for 20-30 year floods, but farmer compensation remains contested.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study based on EPI-WATER and Ungvári and Kis (2022)

sources.note: Climate-ADAPT REST record: regulation history, peak levels, 2004 plan, 721 million m3, six reservoirs 2009-2015 and one in 2022, EUR 260M ERDF and Cohesion Fund, CBA results, compensation limits
